newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Botas seeks 300 km gas pipeline bids.
newsitem.headline: Turk Botas seeks 300 km gas pipeline bids.

text.p: Turkish state-owned pipeline company Botas on Thursday sought bids for the construction of a 300-km (188-mile) natural gas pipeline between the eastern Turkish towns of Erzurum and Dogubeyazit on the Iranian border.

In a statement in Turkey's Official Gazette the company said it was seeking bids by February 28, 1997 for the pipeline, part of a $23-billion, 23-year natural gas deal struck between Turkey and Iran in August.
The Turkish energy ministry has previously said the construction project would cost about $1 billion.
The pipeline will carry an initial three billion cubic metres of Iranian natural gas annually from 1999, to be raised to 10 billion cubic metres from 2005.
The Botas statement said companies or consortiums seeking to take part in the tender may collect tender documents between December 13-25.
It said companies taking part in the tender must have constructed 50 km (31 miles) of pipeline in the past and have constructed industrial plant worth at least $20 million.
